title: 1 Kings 9
paragraphs: ¹ After Solomon had finished building the LORD's house and the royal palace — everything he had desired to do — ² the LORD appeared to him a second time, as he had appeared to him at Gibeon. ³ The LORD said: "I have heard the prayer and the plea you made before me. I have consecrated this house you built by putting my name there forever. My eyes and my heart will always be there. ⁴ As for you, if you walk before me faithfully with integrity of heart, as David your father did, and do all I command and obey my decrees and laws — ⁵ then I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever, as I promised David your father when I said, 'You will never fail to have a successor on the throne of Israel.'"

⁶ "But if you or your children turn away from me and do not obey the commands and decrees I have given you, and instead go and serve other gods and worship them — ⁷ then I will cut off Israel from the land I have given them. I will reject this house I have consecrated for my name, and Israel will become a byword and a mockery among all peoples. ⁸ This house will become a ruin — everyone who passes by will be appalled and will scoff, asking, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and this house?' ⁹ And the answer will be: 'Because they abandoned the LORD their God, who brought their ancestors out of Egypt, and they embraced other gods, worshipping and serving them — that is why the LORD brought all this disaster on them.'" ¹⁰ At the end of twenty years, during which Solomon had built both buildings — the LORD's house and the royal palace —

¹¹ King Solomon gave twenty towns in the region of Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, who had supplied him with all the cedar and juniper and gold he wanted. ¹² But when Hiram came from Tyre to see the towns Solomon had given him, he was not pleased. ¹³ "What kind of towns are these you've given me, my friend?" he said — and he called that region Cabul, the name it still bears. ¹⁴ Hiram had sent the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold. ¹⁵ This is the account of the labor force King Solomon conscripted to build the LORD's house, his own palace, the terraces, the wall of Jerusalem, and the cities of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.

¹⁶ Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked Gezer and captured it, burning it to the ground and killing its Canaanite inhabitants. He gave it as a wedding gift to his daughter, Solomon's wife. ¹⁷ So Solomon rebuilt Gezer and Lower Beth Horon, ¹⁸ as well as Baalath and Tadmor in the desert within his territory, ¹⁹ along with all the cities he used for supplies, the cities for his chariots, the cities for his cavalry, and whatever else he desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout all his kingdom. ²⁰ All the peoples left from the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites — those who were not Israelites —

²¹ the descendants who remained in the land, whom Israel had not been able to destroy — Solomon conscripted them for forced labor, and their descendants remain in that service to this day. ²² But Solomon did not make slaves of any Israelites. They served as his soldiers, officials, officers, commanders, and as captains of his chariots and cavalry. ²³ Five hundred and fifty officials supervised Solomon's projects and directed the workers who carried out the work. ²⁴ After Pharaoh's daughter moved from the City of David to the palace Solomon had built for her, Solomon constructed the terraces. ²⁵ Three times a year Solomon sacrificed burnt offerings and fellowship offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD, along with incense offerings before the LORD. And with that, the temple was complete.

²⁶ King Solomon also built a fleet of ships at Ezion Geber, near Elath on the shore of the Red Sea, in the land of Edom. ²⁷ Hiram sent his own experienced sailors to serve in the fleet alongside Solomon's men. ²⁸ They sailed to Ophir and brought back four hundred and twenty talents of gold, which they delivered to King Solomon.
